headline: IAM policy change grants app wildcard S3 access instead of scoped access

findings.evidence_ref: In iam.tf, the policy Resource field is being changed from ["arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-data", "arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-data/*"] to ["*"]. This change allows the application role to GetObject, PutObject, and ListBucket on all S3 resources in the account.
findings.explanation: This change grants the app EC2 instances broad permissions to read from and write to any S3 bucket in the account—not just the intended acme-prod-data bucket. The app can now access the artifacts bucket (with lifecycle-deleted content) and the static site bucket (public marketing assets), plus any future buckets. This violates the principle of least privilege and creates a significant blast radius if the app is compromised or misconfigured. The stated problem (pager fatigue from adding new buckets) should be solved with better operational processes or resource-based policies, not wildcard IAM permissions.
